newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-Analysts see Skoda losses mounting.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Analysts see Skoda losses mounting.

text.p: Results showing that 1996 unconsolidated net losses at Czech engineering group Skoda a.s. narrowed last year did little to impress analysts who said on Wednesday the consolidated result would be much worse.

The Plzen-based Skoda said unconsolidated losses of the parent company narrowed to 190.281 million crowns ($5.5 million) from 294.575 million crowns in 1995, but that did not include results from any subsidiaries, such as the recently acquired cash-strapped truckmakers Liaz a.s. and Tatra a.s..

Czech equities analysts said that Skoda, which is not affiliated with the carmaker Skoda Automobilova a.s., would post a consolidated 1996 net loss of as much as 700 million crowns due to the acquisition costs of the ailing truck firms.
"These two (truckmakers) are so much trouble for the whole concern Skoda that we expect the 1996 consolidated loss of 600-700 million crowns," said Tomas Navratil of Akro Capital.
Several analysts contacted by Reuters said the acquisitions would cut into Skoda's earnings for years to come.
"I expect a net loss of half a billion crowns," said Miloslav Hruby, equity analyst at Komercni Banka in Prague.

Skoda, which earlier this year forecast 1996 net profit at between nil and 100 million crowns, has yet to file its audited consolidated results for last year or its first-quarter results for this year.
The consolidated results may come next week, a Skoda official told Reuters on Wednesday. The official declined comment on the further outlook for results.
The company has numerous subsidiaries making a range of products from aluminium cans to nuclear power components.
"Huge losses in several subsidiary companies and generally high fixed costs are the main reasons (for the losses)," said Ondrej Datka of Patria Finance.
Patria has forecast Skoda's net 1996 consolidated loss at 520 million crowns.
"We consider this stock as overvalued and have changed our recommendation from a hold to a sell," Datka said in a report to investors.
The firm had a net loss of 432 million crowns in 1995 after a net profit of 91 million crowns the previous year. Sales for 1995 grew to 27 billion crowns from 17 billion.
Skoda shares fell six crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange on Wednesday to close at 980 crowns.
